established_findings: New baseline without recording/writing reproduced positive ~66.7ms intervals for BOTH wrists. Matching hardware timestamp steps and V4L2 sequence skips must be used to distinguish these from timestamp conversion jumps.
Earlier head global-time regression by 534.425ms is a separate confirmed software time-mapping issue; a clean new window does not negate the earlier directly observed event.

Some 100ms selected source intervals arise from 30Hz-to-20Hz nearest-exposure pairing even when original camera frames were all received; see each selected_sample_break_analysis entry rather than equating every segment boundary with hardware loss.

During the new 120s full recording, kernel RGB sequence skips were head=0, left=4, right=5; additionally each camera had one interior RCL publish returning success without a corresponding recorder receive callback. These are two distinct missing-frame stages.

Three segment boundaries in this test are attributable to selected simulated joint samples exceeding 80ms; they are not evidence of actual arm state publication faults, because no physical arm clients or services were used.
The head camera also emitted a startup Left MIPI error hardware notification. This names the head camera internal sensor path, not the left robot arm; its root cause is not established.
Camera/USB/UVC input-stage loss does not by itself prove a defective camera, insufficient power, or insufficient Jetson CPU. Exact physical component remains unisolated.

references.relevance: Official RealSense support notes that this hardware notification alone does not identify its root cause; log occurrence is our own measurement.
